add.content: First-principles alloying predictions linked electronic structure to a brittle-to-ductile transition.
add.evidence_span: First-principles calculations showed that alloying intrinsically brittle Mo and W with subgroup IV or V transition metals can make them intrinsically ductile

add.content: Electronic-structure changes induce Jahn-Teller distortions and shift elastic failure from tension to shear.
add.evidence_span: This composition-induced brittle to ductile transition was explained by changes in the electronic structure, which induced Jahn-Teller distortions and transitioned the elastic instability mode from tensile to shear failure

add.content: The single-phase BCC condition exceeds 60% compressive strain at 1065 MPa yield strength.
add.evidence_span: In Condition (2), the alloy was very ductile at room temperature and did not show any evidence of fracture even after a true strain of 60%, with a noticeably lower yield stress ( σ 0.2 = 1065 MPa).

add.content: Competing B2 slip systems may produce anomalous high-temperature strengthening.
add.evidence_span: the unusual compositional complexity of the B2 phase in the present study may enable two or more different slip systems to compete

add.content: The inverted condition strengthens by about 6% at 600 degrees C, beyond measurement uncertainty.
add.evidence_span: The magnitude of the increase shown in the present work is about 6%, which is significantly larger than a typical sample-to-sample experimental uncertainty of ± 1%.

add.content: BCC and B2 phases partition strongly into distinct compositions.
add.evidence_span: The approximate compositions of the two phases are: BCC: 5Al-27Nb-18Ta-11Zr-33Ti-6V (at%) and B2: 20Al-10Nb-4Ta-31Zr-31Ti-4V (at%).
